Actionable Recommendations:


1. Revert or hotfix release-4.20 PR #617 (fd6ff1e, vitus133/upstream-sync-2026-06-30, merged June 30 2026). The skipInitialStartup phc2sys delay and processWithParser refactoring are the prime suspects for suppressing or altering the log lines that test regexes in main depend on. Verify by checking whether printWhenNotNil() / applyNodePTPProfiles() log output format changed.

2. Retry the periodic job once to distinguish transient lab hardware issues (GNSS on cnfdf32, NIC flap) from the software regression. If the log-stream timeouts recur but a fresh job before June 30 did not have them, that confirms PR #617 as the regression.

3. Inspect linuxptp-daemon pod logs directly on a live cluster for pods bxx22/kbzr7 after the retry: look for ptp4l … LISTENING without a subsequent SLAVE/LOCKED transition, and check whether Profile Name: lines are still emitted at daemon startup — if they are absent, the parser refactor changed log format and test regexes need updating to match.


Overall Issue Class: test_regression (primary — PR #617 in release-4.20 image regresses log output format relied on by main-branch tests), with a possible secondary infra_other component for the tgm GNSS/T-GM hardware state.


Overall Severity: CRITICAL — 26/26 failures (100% of the job) are attributable to the same root cause; the entire nightly 4.20 PTP e2e suite is non-functional.




Per-Suite Details



dualfollower



Suite: dualfollower (4 failures)


Suite TL;DR: All 4 dualfollower test failures are caused by the linuxptp-daemon-container not producing expected PTP sync log output — indicating the PTP hardware synchronization chain never established on the test nodes, a systemic infrastructure failure that affected every test suite in this job run (33 matching failures across bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, tgm).


Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: PTP daemon not producing sync log output (affects: "Slave can sync to master", "Dual follower can sync when one follower port goes down", "Can provide a profile with higher priority")
• Evidence:

```

could not get any profile line, err=could not find regex in log stream for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-wkbsm container=linuxptp-daemon-container, err=error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded

```

```

could not get any profile line, err=could not find regex in log stream for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-wkbsm container=linuxptp-daemon-container, err=timedout waiting for matches

```

All three serial tests time out after ~201s with exactly this error, targeting pod linuxptp-daemon-wkbsm, container linuxptp-daemon-container.

• Root Cause: The test helper (ptphelper.go:GetForeignClockID) streams logs from the linuxptp-daemon-container and searches for PTP profile/sync lines (e.g., master offset ... s2 freq ... produced by ptp4l when in S2/locked state). These lines never appear within the 200s window because ptp4l on the slave node never achieved clock synchronization — it never received a valid grandmaster signal. The same error pattern appears across 33 test failures in 6 suites (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, tgm), all on different pods/nodes, conclusively ruling out a per-config software bug and pointing to a physical/infrastructure-layer failure (GM hardware unavailable, NIC timing signal absent, or hardware link issue on the telco5g lab rack).
• Breaking PR/Commit: Unknown — not a software regression. The job runs test scripts from main against release-4.20 images (PTP_UNDER_TEST_BRANCH=release-4.20, IMG_VERSION=release-4.20), and images built successfully. No per-suite code change is implicated.
• Is it a flake? Yes — transient infrastructure failure in the telco5g lab hardware environment. Confirmed by investigation-summary.txt: "Fix type: infra — Infrastructure issue — likely transient. Retry the job."
• Suggested Fix: Retry the periodic job; if the failure recurs across multiple consecutive runs on the same lab, investigate the telco5g PTP grandmaster hardware (cnfdf30/31/32 rack timing cards, GPS/GNSS signal, or NIC firmware) for the ens2f0 follower interface reported in test config discovery.

• Group 2: OS Clock never LOCKED (affects: "Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync")
• Evidence:

```

OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out

```

(from junit-failures.txt, test: [dualfollower-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)

Supporting: AfterSuite discovery shows PtpEventsIsConsumerReady= false and DiscoveredMasterInterfaces=[]

• Root Cause: The parallel events test polls the OS clock state (via phc2sys metrics or PTP event consumer) waiting for a LOCKED state transition. Because the underlying PTP sync chain failed (same root cause as Group 1 — no GM signal), phc2sys never synchronized the system clock to the PHC, and the OS clock state never transitioned from FREERUN/HOLDOVER to LOCKED within the test timeout. The PtpEventsIsConsumerReady= false in the suite discovery output corroborates that the events subsystem itself was in a degraded state at end-of-run.
• Breaking PR/Commit: Unknown — same infrastructure root cause as Group 1.
• Is it a flake? Yes — same transient lab hardware condition as Group 1.
• Suggested Fix: Same as Group 1; retry the job. If PtpEventsIsConsumerReady remains false across retries, also check the cloud-event-proxy sidecar deployment on the dualfollower node.

Suite Issue Class: infra_other

Suite Severity: LOW

1. Backport linuxptp-daemon main PR #617 to release-4.20 (fixes 11/13 failures). The commit fd6ff1e adds *configInput = configOutput and the unconditional printNodeProfile call that emits Ptp4lConf: #profile: into daemon logs. Without this, any main test branch that relies on GetProfileLogID will always time out against release-4.20 images. Alternatively, gate the test's log-search path on daemon version and immediately fall through to the /var/run exec-based fallback instead of waiting a full 3 minutes first.

2. Investigate T-GM DPLL holdover regression on release-4.20 (fixes 2/13 failures). Audit recent commits to linuxptp-daemon/release-4.20 and cloud-event-proxy/release-4.20 for changes in pkg/event/event.go DPLL state-transition logic. Also verify WPC hardware firmware version matches the expected holdover capability; if firmware is the variable, pin firmware version in the CI telco5g cluster.

3. Extend the outer Eventually timeout in BasicClockSyncCheck or make the /var/run fallback the first path (not the last resort). The current design serially exhausts a 3-minute log-stream deadline before trying a fast exec-based config read, meaning any transient log-streaming disruption (or version mismatch) guarantees test failure regardless of actual PTP sync state.

(The dominant failure mode — 11/13 — is caused by main test code depending on a daemon log line that exists only in main, not in the release-4.20 images the job is actually testing. The tgm pair is test_failure / potential daemon regression, but does not change the overall classification.)

Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: GetProfileLogID log pattern absent from release-4.20 linuxptp-daemon (affects: all 3 tests — "Slave can sync to master", "Downstream slave can sync to BC master", "Can provide a profile with higher priority")
• Evidence:

The same error occurs across all four suites (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha) on different pods (-g59s2, -7khz9, -68lc9, -d75dq), confirming a daemon-wide, systematic failure.


• Root Cause: GetClockIDForeign (called from BasicClockSyncCheck in test/pkg/ptptesthelper/ptptesthelper.go:66) first calls GetProfileLogID (test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go:84), which searches for the regex (?m).?Ptp4lConf: #profile: (.|\n)?message_tag \[(.)\] in the linuxptp-daemon-container logs. This pattern is only emitted when the linuxptp-daemon calls printNodeProfile(nodeProfile) after configInput = configOutput (linuxptp-daemon/pkg/daemon/daemon.go:1152-1154) writes the rendered config (containing #profile: ) back into nodeProfile.Ptp4lConf. Both the *configInput = configOutput assignment and the unconditional printNodeProfile call at line 1412 were introduced in linuxptp-daemon main PR #617 (commit fd6ff1e, merged June 30 2026), but have not been backported to release-4.20. The /var/run-based fallback (GetConfigForProfileFromVarRun, added in ptp-operator main commit 84723c8 June 22) is invoked only after GetProfileLogID's own 3-minute deadline elapses (~t=200s), which coincides with the outer Eventually timeout (3 min), leaving insufficient time to complete exec commands inside the pod and verify the result. GetClockIDForeign then returns lastErr from the log scan, and Eventually reports failure at ~202s.

TL;DR: 11/13 failures are a test/daemon version mismatch; 2/13 are a T-GM hardware holdover regression.



Root Cause Groups:


• 11/13 failures — Ptp4lConf: #profile: log line absent from release-4.20 daemon (bc: 3, dualfollower: 3, dualnicbc: 3, dualnicbcha: 2)

The test helper GetProfileLogID (test code running from main) searches for a log regex (Ptp4lConf: #profile: ) that is only emitted after *configInput = configOutput + printNodeProfile — code introduced in linuxptp-daemon main PR #617 (commit fd6ff1e, merged 2026-06-30) and not backported to release-4.20. The CI job deploys release-4.20 daemon images (USE_UPSTREAM=false), so the pattern is never logged. GetProfileLogID's internal 3-minute deadline consumes the entire outer Eventually window, leaving the /var/run fallback no time to run. All failures surface as either timedout waiting for matches (stream alive, pattern never appeared) or context deadline exceeded (Kubernetes log-stream dropped), with a secondary cluster-API Unauthorized state observed post-run in dualnicbc/dualnicbcha, consistent with infrastructure stress from 11 concurrent 200-second stream-read timeouts.


• 2/13 failures — T-GM DPLL does not enter holdover on GNSS disruption (tgm: 2)

When GNSS signal is lost or rebooted on WPC T-GM hardware, the Intel DPLL is expected to transition to lockStatus: holdover (clock class 7). Instead, the DPLL stays in or falls directly to FREERUN (clock class 248), so openshift_ptp_clock_class never reaches 7. Both tgm tests fail: one by timeout polling for clock class 7, one by direct metric assertion finding 248. This is independent of the log-line issue; the release-4.20 daemon or underlying firmware may have a regression in holdover state management.

TL;DR: All 26 failures stem from linuxptp-daemon (release-4.20) never achieving PTP clock sync, likely triggered by PR #617.



Root Cause Groups:


• 23/26 failures — linuxptp-daemon log-stream regex timeouts (PTP sync never achieved): Tests across all 6 suites (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, tgm) stream logs from linuxptp-daemon-container waiting for ptp4l sync lines that never appear. Pods implicated: f2rj4, m8sk4, wkbsm, xpbz5, bxx22, ncr6h, kbzr7, cngvw. Errors: timedout waiting for matches / context deadline exceeded. All suites are affected; no suite was spared.

• 3/26 failures — T-GM on cnfdf32 stuck in ClockClass 248 (FREERUN): All three tgm tests failed because the WPC T-GM grandmaster (node cnfdf32, interface ens7fx/master) never achieved GNSS lock (ClockClass 7). Prometheus metric confirms ClockClass=248 throughout. This is either a cascade from the same daemon regression or an independent GNSS/hardware issue on that node.


Cross-Suite Patterns:


SuiteRoot CauseSuite-specific?
dualfollowerLog-stream timeout (pod wkbsm)No
dualnicbcLog-stream timeout (pod xpbz5)No
dualnicbchaLog-stream timeout (pods bxx22, ncr6h)No — but dualnicbcha analysis fingered PR #617 most explicitly

All suites share the core log-stream regex failure. The tgm FREERUN failures are superficially different but may be downstream of the same daemon regression (ts2phc log parsing altered by PR #617).



Actionable Recommendations:


1. Revert or hotfix release-4.20 PR #617 (fd6ff1e, vitus133/upstream-sync-2026-06-30, merged June 30 2026). The skipInitialStartup phc2sys delay and processWithParser refactoring are the prime suspects for suppressing or altering the log lines that test regexes in main depend on. Verify by checking whether printWhenNotNil() / applyNodePTPProfiles() log output format changed.

2. Retry the periodic job once to distinguish transient lab hardware issues (GNSS on cnfdf32, NIC flap) from the software regression. If the log-stream timeouts recur but a fresh job before June 30 did not have them, that confirms PR #617 as the regression.

3. Inspect linuxptp-daemon pod logs directly on a live cluster for pods bxx22/kbzr7 after the retry: look for ptp4l … LISTENING without a subsequent SLAVE/LOCKED transition, and check whether Profile Name: lines are still emitted at daemon startup — if they are absent, the parser refactor changed log format and test regexes need updating to match.


Overall Issue Class: test_regression (primary — PR #617 in release-4.20 image regresses log output format relied on by main-branch tests), with a possible secondary infra_other component for the tgm GNSS/T-GM hardware state.


Overall Severity: CRITICAL — 26/26 failures (100% of the job) are attributable to the same root cause; the entire nightly 4.20 PTP e2e suite is non-functional.




Per-Suite Details



dualfollower



Suite: dualfollower (4 failures)


Suite TL;DR: All 4 dualfollower test failures are caused by the linuxptp-daemon-container not producing expected PTP sync log output — indicating the PTP hardware synchronization chain never established on the test nodes, a systemic infrastructure failure that affected every test suite in this job run (33 matching failures across bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, tgm).


Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: PTP daemon not producing sync log output (affects: "Slave can sync to master", "Dual follower can sync when one follower port goes down", "Can provide a profile with higher priority")
• Evidence:

```

could not get any profile line, err=could not find regex in log stream for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-wkbsm container=linuxptp-daemon-container, err=error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded

```

```

could not get any profile line, err=could not find regex in log stream for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-wkbsm container=linuxptp-daemon-container, err=timedout waiting for matches

```

All three serial tests time out after ~201s with exactly this error, targeting pod linuxptp-daemon-wkbsm, container linuxptp-daemon-container.

• Root Cause: The test helper (ptphelper.go:GetForeignClockID) streams logs from the linuxptp-daemon-container and searches for PTP profile/sync lines (e.g., master offset ... s2 freq ... produced by ptp4l when in S2/locked state). These lines never appear within the 200s window because ptp4l on the slave node never achieved clock synchronization — it never received a valid grandmaster signal. The same error pattern appears across 33 test failures in 6 suites (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, tgm), all on different pods/nodes, conclusively ruling out a per-config software bug and pointing to a physical/infrastructure-layer failure (GM hardware unavailable, NIC timing signal absent, or hardware link issue on the telco5g lab rack).
• Breaking PR/Commit: Unknown — not a software regression. The job runs test scripts from main against release-4.20 images (PTP_UNDER_TEST_BRANCH=release-4.20, IMG_VERSION=release-4.20), and images built successfully. No per-suite code change is implicated.
• Is it a flake? Yes — transient infrastructure failure in the telco5g lab hardware environment. Confirmed by investigation-summary.txt: "Fix type: infra — Infrastructure issue — likely transient. Retry the job."
• Suggested Fix: Retry the periodic job; if the failure recurs across multiple consecutive runs on the same lab, investigate the telco5g PTP grandmaster hardware (cnfdf30/31/32 rack timing cards, GPS/GNSS signal, or NIC firmware) for the ens2f0 follower interface reported in test config discovery.

• Group 2: OS Clock never LOCKED (affects: "Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync")
• Evidence:

```

OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out

```

(from junit-failures.txt, test: [dualfollower-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)

Supporting: AfterSuite discovery shows PtpEventsIsConsumerReady= false and DiscoveredMasterInterfaces=[]

• Root Cause: The parallel events test polls the OS clock state (via phc2sys metrics or PTP event consumer) waiting for a LOCKED state transition. Because the underlying PTP sync chain failed (same root cause as Group 1 — no GM signal), phc2sys never synchronized the system clock to the PHC, and the OS clock state never transitioned from FREERUN/HOLDOVER to LOCKED within the test timeout. The PtpEventsIsConsumerReady= false in the suite discovery output corroborates that the events subsystem itself was in a degraded state at end-of-run.
• Breaking PR/Commit: Unknown — same infrastructure root cause as Group 1.
• Is it a flake? Yes — same transient lab hardware condition as Group 1.
• Suggested Fix: Same as Group 1; retry the job. If PtpEventsIsConsumerReady remains false across retries, also check the cloud-event-proxy sidecar deployment on the dualfollower node.

Suite Issue Class: infra_other

Suite Severity: LOW

dualfollower



Suite: dualfollower (4 failures)


Suite TL;DR: All 4 dualfollower test failures are caused by the linuxptp-daemon-container not producing expected PTP sync log output — indicating the PTP hardware synchronization chain never established on the test nodes, a systemic infrastructure failure that affected every test suite in this job run (33 matching failures across bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, tgm).


Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: PTP daemon not producing sync log output (affects: "Slave can sync to master", "Dual follower can sync when one follower port goes down", "Can provide a profile with higher priority")
• Evidence:

```

could not get any profile line, err=could not find regex in log stream for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-wkbsm container=linuxptp-daemon-container, err=error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded

```

```

could not get any profile line, err=could not find regex in log stream for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-wkbsm container=linuxptp-daemon-container, err=timedout waiting for matches

```

All three serial tests time out after ~201s with exactly this error, targeting pod linuxptp-daemon-wkbsm, container linuxptp-daemon-container.

• Root Cause: The test helper (ptphelper.go:GetForeignClockID) streams logs from the linuxptp-daemon-container and searches for PTP profile/sync lines (e.g., master offset ... s2 freq ... produced by ptp4l when in S2/locked state). These lines never appear within the 200s window because ptp4l on the slave node never achieved clock synchronization — it never received a valid grandmaster signal. The same error pattern appears across 33 test failures in 6 suites (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, tgm), all on different pods/nodes, conclusively ruling out a per-config software bug and pointing to a physical/infrastructure-layer failure (GM hardware unavailable, NIC timing signal absent, or hardware link issue on the telco5g lab rack).
• Breaking PR/Commit: Unknown — not a software regression. The job runs test scripts from main against release-4.20 images (PTP_UNDER_TEST_BRANCH=release-4.20, IMG_VERSION=release-4.20), and images built successfully. No per-suite code change is implicated.
• Is it a flake? Yes — transient infrastructure failure in the telco5g lab hardware environment. Confirmed by investigation-summary.txt: "Fix type: infra — Infrastructure issue — likely transient. Retry the job."
• Suggested Fix: Retry the periodic job; if the failure recurs across multiple consecutive runs on the same lab, investigate the telco5g PTP grandmaster hardware (cnfdf30/31/32 rack timing cards, GPS/GNSS signal, or NIC firmware) for the ens2f0 follower interface reported in test config discovery.

• Group 2: OS Clock never LOCKED (affects: "Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync")
• Evidence:

```

OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out

```

(from junit-failures.txt, test: [dualfollower-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)

Supporting: AfterSuite discovery shows PtpEventsIsConsumerReady= false and DiscoveredMasterInterfaces=[]

• Root Cause: The parallel events test polls the OS clock state (via phc2sys metrics or PTP event consumer) waiting for a LOCKED state transition. Because the underlying PTP sync chain failed (same root cause as Group 1 — no GM signal), phc2sys never synchronized the system clock to the PHC, and the OS clock state never transitioned from FREERUN/HOLDOVER to LOCKED within the test timeout. The PtpEventsIsConsumerReady= false in the suite discovery output corroborates that the events subsystem itself was in a degraded state at end-of-run.
• Breaking PR/Commit: Unknown — same infrastructure root cause as Group 1.
• Is it a flake? Yes — same transient lab hardware condition as Group 1.
• Suggested Fix: Same as Group 1; retry the job. If PtpEventsIsConsumerReady remains false across retries, also check the cloud-event-proxy sidecar deployment on the dualfollower node.

The test helper GetProfileLogID (test code running from main) searches for a log regex (Ptp4lConf: #profile: ) that is only emitted after *configInput = configOutput + printNodeProfile — code introduced in linuxptp-daemon main PR #617 (commit fd6ff1e, merged 2026-06-30) and not backported to release-4.20. The CI job deploys release-4.20 daemon images (USE_UPSTREAM=false), so the pattern is never logged. GetProfileLogID's internal 3-minute deadline consumes the entire outer Eventually window, leaving the /var/run fallback no time to run. All failures surface as either timedout waiting for matches (stream alive, pattern never appeared) or context deadline exceeded (Kubernetes log-stream dropped), with a secondary cluster-API Unauthorized state observed post-run in dualnicbc/dualnicbcha, consistent with infrastructure stress from 11 concurrent 200-second stream-read timeouts.


• 2/13 failures — T-GM DPLL does not enter holdover on GNSS disruption (tgm: 2)

When GNSS signal is lost or rebooted on WPC T-GM hardware, the Intel DPLL is expected to transition to lockStatus: holdover (clock class 7). Instead, the DPLL stays in or falls directly to FREERUN (clock class 248), so openshift_ptp_clock_class never reaches 7. Both tgm tests fail: one by timeout polling for clock class 7, one by direct metric assertion finding 248. This is independent of the log-line issue; the release-4.20 daemon or underlying firmware may have a regression in holdover state management.



Cross-Suite Patterns:


Root CauseSuites AffectedFailures
#profile: log line missing from release-4.20 daemonbc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha11
T-GM DPLL does not enter holdover (clock class 7)tgm2

The 11-failure group is fully cross-suite: all four PTP topology suites hit identical pod-log-stream errors on six different pods across different nodes, ruling out any single pod, node, or suite-specific cause. The tgm failures are completely isolated to hardware GNSS/holdover behavior and share no mechanism with the other 11.



Actionable Recommendations:


1. Backport linuxptp-daemon main PR #617 to release-4.20 (fixes 11/13 failures). The commit fd6ff1e adds *configInput = configOutput and the unconditional printNodeProfile call that emits Ptp4lConf: #profile: into daemon logs. Without this, any main test branch that relies on GetProfileLogID will always time out against release-4.20 images. Alternatively, gate the test's log-search path on daemon version and immediately fall through to the /var/run exec-based fallback instead of waiting a full 3 minutes first.

2. Investigate T-GM DPLL holdover regression on release-4.20 (fixes 2/13 failures). Audit recent commits to linuxptp-daemon/release-4.20 and cloud-event-proxy/release-4.20 for changes in pkg/event/event.go DPLL state-transition logic. Also verify WPC hardware firmware version matches the expected holdover capability; if firmware is the variable, pin firmware version in the CI telco5g cluster.

3. Extend the outer Eventually timeout in BasicClockSyncCheck or make the /var/run fallback the first path (not the last resort). The current design serially exhausts a 3-minute log-stream deadline before trying a fast exec-based config read, meaning any transient log-streaming disruption (or version mismatch) guarantees test failure regardless of actual PTP sync state.


Overall Issue Class: test_regression

(The dominant failure mode — 11/13 — is caused by main test code depending on a daemon log line that exists only in main, not in the release-4.20 images the job is actually testing. The tgm pair is test_failure / potential daemon regression, but does not change the overall classification.)


Overall Severity: HIGH

(11/13 failures are systemic and reproducible across every topology suite in every run that pairs main test scripts with release-4.20 daemon images; the job cannot pass in this configuration without the backport or a test-side workaround.)

The same error occurs across all four suites (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha) on different pods (-g59s2, -7khz9, -68lc9, -d75dq), confirming a daemon-wide, systematic failure.


• Root Cause: GetClockIDForeign (called from BasicClockSyncCheck in test/pkg/ptptesthelper/ptptesthelper.go:66) first calls GetProfileLogID (test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go:84), which searches for the regex (?m).?Ptp4lConf: #profile: (.|\n)?message_tag \[(.)\] in the linuxptp-daemon-container logs. This pattern is only emitted when the linuxptp-daemon calls printNodeProfile(nodeProfile) after configInput = configOutput (linuxptp-daemon/pkg/daemon/daemon.go:1152-1154) writes the rendered config (containing #profile: ) back into nodeProfile.Ptp4lConf. Both the *configInput = configOutput assignment and the unconditional printNodeProfile call at line 1412 were introduced in linuxptp-daemon main PR #617 (commit fd6ff1e, merged June 30 2026), but have not been backported to release-4.20. The CI job runs test scripts from ptp-operator main against release-4.20 production images, so the daemon never emits the expected log line. The /var/run-based fallback (GetConfigForProfileFromVarRun, added in ptp-operator main commit 84723c8 June 22) is invoked only after GetProfileLogID's own 3-minute deadline elapses (~t=200s), which coincides with the outer Eventually timeout (3 min), leaving insufficient time to complete exec commands inside the pod and verify the result. GetClockIDForeign then returns lastErr from the log scan, and Eventually reports failure at ~202s.

• Breaking PR/Commit: linuxptp-daemon main PR #617 (fd6ff1e, June 30 2026) added *configInput = configOutput and the unconditional printNodeProfile that the test requires — but this has not been cherry-picked to release-4.20. Per branch-awareness policy, a main-only change cannot be the root cause; the true underlying issue is that the main test code (GetProfileLogID, introduced in ptp-operator commit 73a75ec, March 25 2026) was written assuming a log-output behavior that exists only on main linuxptp-daemon, not in release-4.20 images. Secondary contributing commit: ptp-operator bb43e35 (June 23 2026) has prerequisite k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon#215 which also affects daemon startup behavior


TL;DR: All 26 failures stem from linuxptp-daemon (release-4.20) never achieving PTP clock sync, likely triggered by PR #617.



Root Cause Groups:


• 23/26 failures — linuxptp-daemon log-stream regex timeouts (PTP sync never achieved): Tests across all 6 suites (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, tgm) stream logs from linuxptp-daemon-container waiting for ptp4l sync lines that never appear. Pods implicated: f2rj4, m8sk4, wkbsm, xpbz5, bxx22, ncr6h, kbzr7, cngvw. Errors: timedout waiting for matches / context deadline exceeded. All suites are affected; no suite was spared.

• 3/26 failures — T-GM on cnfdf32 stuck in ClockClass 248 (FREERUN): All three tgm tests failed because the WPC T-GM grandmaster (node cnfdf32, interface ens7fx/master) never achieved GNSS lock (ClockClass 7). Prometheus metric confirms ClockClass=248 throughout. This is either a cascade from the same daemon regression or an independent GNSS/hardware issue on that node.

Suite: dualfollower (4 failures)


Suite TL;DR: All 4 dualfollower test failures are caused by the linuxptp-daemon-container not producing expected PTP sync log output — indicating the PTP hardware synchronization chain never established on the test nodes, a systemic infrastructure failure that affected every test suite in this job run (33 matching failures across bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, tgm).


Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: PTP daemon not producing sync log output (affects: "Slave can sync to master", "Dual follower can sync when one follower port goes down", "Can provide a profile with higher priority")
• Evidence:

```

could not get any profile line, err=could not find regex in log stream for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-wkbsm container=linuxptp-daemon-container, err=error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded

```

```

could not get any profile line, err=could not find regex in log stream for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-wkbsm container=linuxptp-daemon-container, err=timedout waiting for matches

```

All three serial tests time out after ~201s with exactly this error, targeting pod linuxptp-daemon-wkbsm, container linuxptp-daemon-container.

• Root Cause: The test helper (ptphelper.go:GetForeignClockID) streams logs from the linuxptp-daemon-container and searches for PTP profile/sync lines (e.g., master offset ... s2 freq ... produced by ptp4l when in S2/locked state). These lines never appear within the 200s window because ptp4l on the slave node never achieved clock synchronization — it never received a valid grandmaster signal. The same error pattern appears across 33 test failures in 6 suites (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, tgm), all on different pods/nodes, conclusively ruling out a per-config software bug and pointing to a physical/infrastructure-layer failure (GM hardware unavailable, NIC timing signal absent, or hardware link issue on the telco5g lab rack).
• Breaking PR/Commit: Unknown — not a software regression. The job runs test scripts from main against release-4.20 images (PTP_UNDER_TEST_BRANCH=release-4.20, IMG_VERSION=release-4.20), and images built successfully. No per-suite code change is implicated.
• Is it a flake? Yes — transient infrastructure failure in the telco5g lab hardware environment. Confirmed by investigation-summary.txt: "Fix type: infra — Infrastructure issue — likely transient. Retry the job."
• Suggested Fix: Retry the periodic job; if the failure recurs across multiple consecutive runs on the same lab, investigate the telco5g PTP grandmaster hardware (cnfdf30/31/32 rack timing cards, GPS/GNSS signal, or NIC firmware) for the ens2f0 follower interface reported in test config discovery.

• Group 2: OS Clock never LOCKED (affects: "Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync")
• Evidence:

```

OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out

```

(from junit-failures.txt, test: [dualfollower-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)

Supporting: AfterSuite discovery shows PtpEventsIsConsumerReady= false and DiscoveredMasterInterfaces=[]

• Root Cause: The parallel events test polls the OS clock state (via phc2sys metrics or PTP event consumer) waiting for a LOCKED state transition. Because the underlying PTP sync chain failed (same root cause as Group 1 — no GM signal), phc2sys never synchronized the system clock to the PHC, and the OS clock state never transitioned from FREERUN/HOLDOVER to LOCKED within the test timeout. The PtpEventsIsConsumerReady= false in the suite discovery output corroborates that the events subsystem itself was in a degraded state at end-of-run.
• Breaking PR/Commit: Unknown — same infrastructure root cause as Group 1.
• Is it a flake? Yes — same transient lab hardware condition as Group 1.
• Suggested Fix: Same as Group 1; retry the job. If PtpEventsIsConsumerReady remains false across retries, also check the cloud-event-proxy sidecar deployment on the dualfollower node.

• ~22/26 failures — PTP grandmaster never achieved lock; serial log-stream tests timed out

This is the direct, unambiguous confirmation of the same root cause: the entire clock hierarchy (grandmaster → BC → slave) failed to converge.

• 22/26 failures — PTP lock never achieved; linuxptp-daemon log stream regex never matches (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha serial tests, plus tbc/tgm suites referenced in cross-suite evidence)

Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: linuxptp-daemon log stream read timeout (affects: "PTP ClockSync Slave can sync to master [Serial]", "PTP ClockSync Downstream slave can sync to BC master [Serial]", "PTP ClockSync Can provide a profile with higher priority [Serial]")
• Evidence:

```

Cross-suite confirmation (dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc — all suites): identical could not find regex in log stream errors on every linuxptp-daemon pod.

• Root Cause: The test framework (ptp-operator-conformance-test) reads the pod log stream of linuxptp-daemon-container and matches regex patterns to extract a "foreign clock ID" and "profile line" — log output produced only when ptp4l achieves a master-slave PTP relationship and prints selection messages. Because ptp4l never successfully locked to a grandmaster in this run, those log lines never appeared, causing the 204–208 s per-test timeout to fire. The failure is not a code defect in the test regex itself but a genuine failure of PTP synchronization on the worker nodes; this is confirmed by the event-based parallel test below.
• Breaking PR/Commit: Unknown — no release-4.20 source changes were detectable from the cloned repos; the systemic cross-suite pattern (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, tgm all fail identically) makes a single code regression unlikely.
• Is it a flake? yes — all evidence points to a transient lab/hardware condition rather than a reproducible code defect.
• Suggested Fix: Retry the periodic job; if failures recur across consecutive nightly runs, inspect the telco5g lab's GPS receiver and PTP-capable NIC state on cnfdf30/cnfdf31, and collect journalctl / ptp4l logs from inside linuxptp-daemon-container to determine whether ptp4l even started negotiating.

• Group 2: OS Clock never LOCKED (affects: "[bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync")
• Evidence:

```

OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out

```

Full AI Analysis

TL;DR: 13 of 15 failures are a single test flake — a log-rotation race that voids GetProfileLogID; 2 are a WPC T-GM holdover hardware failure.



Root Cause Groups:


• 13/15 failures — GetProfileLogID log-rotation timeout (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc): BasicClockSyncCheck → GetClockIDForeign → GetProfileLogID (ptphelper.go:69) opens a Follow: true log stream and searches for (?m).?Ptp4lConf: #profile: (.|\n)?message_tag \[.*\]. That regex only matches a line emitted once by printNodeProfile at daemon startup. Cluster setup finished at ~02:06; ClockSync tests ran at ~04:00–06:00 (~2–4 h later). By then CRI-O log rotation had cycled the startup entry out of the K8s-served log buffer. The snapshot read yields nothing (~26 s); the follow-stream times out after 180 s — producing the observed ~206–218 s failure duration across every suite. The "Can provide a profile with higher priority" variant adds ~60–90 s of profile-apply wait before hitting the same timeout (yielding ~287–298 s).

• 2/15 failures — WPC T-GM DPLL holdover not sustained (tgm): After GNSS disconnect, ts2phc either never emits the "holdover" log token (test 1 — 3+ min of retries, class stays at 6) or emits class-7 followed 7 ms later by class-248 (test 2 — DPLL flips through holdover and drops to FREERUN before the test can assert it). Root is in the WPC DPLL firmware or the ts2phc_parser.go:162-163 holdover-detection logic, not in the test itself.


Cross-Suite Patterns:


SuiteFailuresRoot Cause
bc3Log rotation (GetProfileLogID)
dualfollower3Log rotation (GetProfileLogID)
dualnicbc3Log rotation (GetProfileLogID)
dualnicbcha2Log rotation (GetProfileLogID) — same 206–218 s signature
oc2Log rotation (GetProfileLogID) — same 206–218 s signature
tgm2WPC T-GM holdover hardware/firmware failure

All five non-tgm suites share an identical root cause and near-identical failure durations. The dualnicbcha and oc per-suite analyses characterize the symptom as "LOCKED state timeout," but the timing signature (206–218 s, 287–298 s) and the GetProfileLogID call stack are identical to bc/dualfollower/dualnicbc. tgm is the only suite with a distinct, hardware-level root cause.



Actionable Recommendations:


1. Fix GetProfileLogID to not depend on rotated startup logs. Instead of parsing the one-shot printNodeProfile startup line, query the current PTP configuration state directly — either from a /metrics endpoint, the PtpConfig CR status, or by triggering a daemon profile-reload (e.g., a no-op annotation update) immediately before the test assertion window. This single fix eliminates 13/15 failures.

2. Investigate the WPC DPLL holdover firmware behavior on cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com. Capture ts2phc raw log output during GNSS disconnect to determine whether the DPLL hardware never enters holdover or enters and exits it within milliseconds. If the latter, check whether the DPLL holdover duration register is being set correctly from ts2phc.holdover config and whether a firmware update is available for the WPC card.

3. Add a canary assertion for daemon log reachability before ClockSync tests. A short pre-check that confirms GetPodLogsRegex can read at least one log line from the daemon container (not the specific startup pattern) would convert a silent 206 s timeout into a fast, labeled skip/infra-failure, making future regressions easier to triage.


Overall Issue Class: test_flake (13/15); infra_other (2/15 tgm)


Overall Severity: MEDIUM — the dominant failure mode is a pre-existing, deterministic time-dependent flake (not a code regression); the tgm failures indicate a real hardware/firmware problem on one lab node but affect only 2 tests.

Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: GetProfileLogID regex never matches — daemon log pattern requires second profile apply (affects: all 3 tests)
• Evidence:

```

[Jun 26 04:03:18.197][ptphelper.go: 123] GetProfileLogID attempt 1 failed for test-bc-master1_test-bc-master1: could not get any profile line, err=could not find regex in log stream for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-nqmpf container=linuxptp-daemon-container, err=error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded, retrying...

[Jun 26 04:04:28.470][ptphelper.go: 123] GetProfileLogID attempt 2 failed for test-bc-master1_test-bc-master1: could not get any profile line, ...context deadline exceeded, retrying...

[Jun 26 04:05:39.315][ptptesthelper.go: 68] GetClockIDForeign retry due to err: could not get any profile line, err=could not find regex in log stream for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-nqmpf container=linuxptp-daemon-container, err=error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded

```

Failure message (Test 1): Timed out after 202.124s. Timeout to get foreign clock ID for ptpconfig test-bc-master1


Failure message (Test 2): Timed out after 202.701s. Timeout to get foreign clock ID for ptpconfig test-slave1 (pod linuxptp-daemon-2vqqd)


Failure message (Test 3): Timed out after 201.746s. Timeout to get foreign clock ID for ptpconfig temp / err=timedout waiting for matches


Cluster setup completed at 02:06:48; ClockSync tests started at 04:02:12 (~1h55m later). The daemon applied profiles ONCE at setup startup and was stable since then.


• Root Cause: GetProfileLogID (ptphelper.go:69) uses the regex (?m).?Ptp4lConf: #profile: %s(.|\n)?message_tag \[(.)\]. This pattern is only logged by printNodeProfile (daemon.go:893) when nodeProfile.Ptp4lConf already contains the RENDERED config (i.e., after configInput = configOutput at daemon.go:1119 has updated the pointer's string on a PREVIOUS apply). On the very first profile application, printNodeProfile logs the RAW CRD config which has NO #profile: header and NO message_tag line — both are added only by RenderPtp4lConf() / ExtendGlobalSection(). Since the daemon applied profiles once at cluster-setup time (~2 hours before tests) and never re-applied them, neither Pass 1 (existing logs) nor Pass 2 (follow stream) in GetPodLogsRegex (pods.go:214) can find the pattern. Test 3 (higher priority profile) also creates a brand-new temp profile that is applied exactly once, so the same structural mismatch applies.

• Breaking PR/Commit: The structural flaw is in GetProfileLogID (ptphelper.go:69) itself — no single commit is the direct trigger. The two-pass GetPodLogsRegex was introduced/modified in commits 0f98a60 and 9c1bc7f; 41f3dd9 (May 11 2026) changed the initial snapshot timeout from 3 min to 1 min but is not the root regression. The underlying issue — that Ptp4lConf: #profile: only appears in logs on the 2nd+ apply — has existed as a latent flake since GetProfileLogID was introduced. Unknown PR for the original introduction; the relevant release branch is release-4.21 in github.com/openshift/ptp-operator.

• Is it a flake? Yes — the test passes when something triggers a second profile application between cluster setup and the ClockSync test window (e.g., operator config reconciliation, hardware config event, daemon restart). In this run, ~2 hours of stability after setup meant no re-apply occurred.

• Suggested Fix: In GetProfileLogID, instead of relying on the Ptp4lConf: log (which requires a second apply), read the ptp4l config file directly from the pod filesystem (/var/run/ptp4l.0.config)

Failure message (Test 1): Timed out after 202.124s. Timeout to get foreign clock ID for ptpconfig test-bc-master1


Failure message (Test 2): Timed out after 202.701s. Timeout to get foreign clock ID for ptpconfig test-slave1 (pod linuxptp-daemon-2vqqd)


Failure message (Test 3): Timed out after 201.746s. Timeout to get foreign clock ID for ptpconfig temp / err=timedout waiting for matches


Cluster setup completed at 02:06:48; ClockSync tests started at 04:02:12 (~1h55m later). The daemon applied profiles ONCE at setup startup and was stable since then.


• Root Cause: GetProfileLogID (ptphelper.go:69) uses the regex (?m).?Ptp4lConf: #profile: %s(.|\n)?message_tag \[(.)\]. This pattern is only logged by printNodeProfile (daemon.go:893) when nodeProfile.Ptp4lConf already contains the RENDERED config (i.e., after configInput = configOutput at daemon.go:1119 has updated the pointer's string on a PREVIOUS apply). On the very first profile application, printNodeProfile logs the RAW CRD config which has NO #profile: header and NO message_tag line — both are added only by RenderPtp4lConf() / ExtendGlobalSection(). Since the daemon applied profiles once at cluster-setup time (~2 hours before tests) and never re-applied them, neither Pass 1 (existing logs) nor Pass 2 (follow stream) in GetPodLogsRegex (pods.go:214) can find the pattern. Test 3 (higher priority profile) also creates a brand-new temp profile that is applied exactly once, so the same structural mismatch applies.

• Breaking PR/Commit: The structural flaw is in GetProfileLogID (ptphelper.go:69) itself — no single commit is the direct trigger. The two-pass GetPodLogsRegex was introduced/modified in commits 0f98a60 and 9c1bc7f; 41f3dd9 (May 11 2026) changed the initial snapshot timeout from 3 min to 1 min but is not the root regression. The underlying issue — that Ptp4lConf: #profile: only appears in logs on the 2nd+ apply — has existed as a latent flake since GetProfileLogID was introduced. Unknown PR for the original introduction; the relevant release branch is release-4.21 in github.com/openshift/ptp-operator.

• Is it a flake? Yes — the test passes when something triggers a second profile application between cluster setup and the ClockSync test window (e.g., operator config reconciliation, hardware config event, daemon restart). In this run, ~2 hours of stability after setup meant no re-apply occurred.

• Suggested Fix: In GetProfileLogID, instead of relying on the Ptp4lConf: log (which requires a second apply), read the ptp4l config file directly from the pod filesystem (/var/run/ptp4l.0.config)


TL;DR: 13 of 15 failures are a single test flake — a log-rotation race that voids GetProfileLogID; 2 are a WPC T-GM holdover hardware failure.



Root Cause Groups:


• 13/15 failures — GetProfileLogID log-rotation timeout (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc): BasicClockSyncCheck → GetClockIDForeign → GetProfileLogID (ptphelper.go:69) opens a Follow: true log stream and searches for (?m).?Ptp4lConf: #profile: (.|\n)?message_tag \[.*\]. That regex only matches a line emitted once by printNodeProfile at daemon startup. Cluster setup finished at ~02:06; ClockSync tests ran at ~04:00–06:00 (~2–4 h later). By then CRI-O log rotation had cycled the startup entry out of the K8s-served log buffer. The snapshot read yields nothing (~26 s); the follow-stream times out after 180 s — producing the observed ~206–218 s failure duration across every suite. The "Can provide a profile with higher priority" variant adds ~60–90 s of profile-apply wait before hitting the same timeout (yielding ~287–298 s).

• 2/15 failures — WPC T-GM DPLL holdover not sustained (tgm): After GNSS disconnect, ts2phc either never emits the "holdover" log token (test 1 — 3+ min of retries, class stays at 6) or emits class-7 followed 7 ms later by class-248 (test 2 — DPLL flips through holdover and drops to FREERUN before the test can assert it). Root is in the WPC DPLL firmware or the ts2phc_parser.go:162-163 holdover-detection logic, not in the test itself.


Cross-Suite Patterns:


SuiteFailuresRoot Cause
bc3Log rotation (GetProfileLogID)
dualfollower3Log rotation (GetProfileLogID)
dualnicbc3Log rotation (GetProfileLogID)
dualnicbcha2Log rotation (GetProfileLogID) — same 206–218 s signature
oc2Log rotation (GetProfileLogID) — same 206–218 s signature
tgm2WPC T-GM holdover hardware/firmware failure

All five non-tgm suites share an identical root cause and near-identical failure durations. The dualnicbcha and oc per-suite analyses characterize the symptom as "LOCKED state timeout," but the timing signature (206–218 s, 287–298 s) and the GetProfileLogID call stack are identical to bc/dualfollower/dualnicbc. tgm is the only suite with a distinct, hardware-level root cause.



Actionable Recommendations:


1. Fix GetProfileLogID to not depend on rotated startup logs. Instead of parsing the one-shot printNodeProfile startup line, query the current PTP configuration state directly — either from a /metrics endpoint, the PtpConfig CR status, or by triggering a daemon profile-reload (e.g., a no-op annotation update) immediately before the test assertion window. This single fix eliminates 13/15 failures.

2. Investigate the WPC DPLL holdover firmware behavior on cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com. Capture ts2phc raw log output during GNSS disconnect to determine whether the DPLL hardware never enters holdover or enters and exits it within milliseconds. If the latter, check whether the DPLL holdover duration register is being set correctly from ts2phc.holdover config and whether a firmware update is available for the WPC card.

3. Add a canary assertion for daemon log reachability before ClockSync tests. A short pre-check that confirms GetPodLogsRegex can read at least one log line from the daemon container (not the specific startup pattern) would convert a silent 206 s timeout into a fast, labeled skip/infra-failure, making future regressions easier to triage.


Overall Issue Class: test_flake (13/15); infra_other (2/15 tgm)


Overall Severity: MEDIUM — the dominant failure mode is a pre-existing, deterministic time-dependent flake (not a code regression); the tgm failures indicate a real hardware/firmware problem on one lab node but affect only 2 tests.

If the latter, check whether the DPLL holdover duration register is being set correctly from ts2phc.holdover config and whether a firmware update is available for the WPC card.

3. Add a canary assertion for daemon log reachability before ClockSync tests. A short pre-check that confirms GetPodLogsRegex can read at least one log line from the daemon container (not the specific startup pattern) would convert a silent 206 s timeout into a fast, labeled skip/infra-failure, making future regressions easier to triage.

• Evidence:

```

[Jun 26 04:03:18.197][ptphelper.go: 123] GetProfileLogID attempt 1 failed for test-bc-master1_test-bc-master1: could not get any profile line, err=could not find regex in log stream for openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon-nqmpf container=linuxptp-daemon-container, err=error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded, retrying...

```

Failure message (Test 1): Timed out after 202.124s. Timeout to get foreign clock ID for ptpconfig test-bc-master1


Failure message (Test 2): Timed out after 202.701s. Timeout to get foreign clock ID for ptpconfig test-slave1 (pod linuxptp-daemon-2vqqd)


Failure message (Test 3): Timed out after 201.746s. Timeout to get foreign clock ID for ptpconfig temp / err=timedout waiting for matches


Cluster setup completed at 02:06:48; ClockSync tests started at 04:02:12 (~1h55m later). The daemon applied profiles ONCE at setup startup and was stable since then.


• Root Cause: GetProfileLogID (ptphelper.go:69) uses the regex (?m).?Ptp4lConf: #profile: %s(.|\n)?message_tag \[(.)\]. This pattern is only logged by printNodeProfile (daemon.go:893) when nodeProfile.Ptp4lConf already contains the RENDERED config (i.e., after configInput = configOutput at daemon.go:1119 has updated the pointer's string on a PREVIOUS apply). On the very first profile application, printNodeProfile logs the RAW CRD config which has NO #profile: header and NO message_tag line — both are added only by RenderPtp4lConf() / ExtendGlobalSection(). Since the daemon applied profiles once at cluster-setup time (~2 hours before tests) and never re-applied them, neither Pass 1 (existing logs) nor Pass 2 (follow stream) in GetPodLogsRegex (pods.go:214) can find the pattern. Test 3 (higher priority profile) also creates a brand-new temp profile that is applied exactly once, so the same structural mismatch applies.

• Breaking PR/Commit: The structural flaw is in GetProfileLogID (ptphelper.go:69) itself — no single commit is the direct trigger. The two-pass GetPodLogsRegex was introduced/modified in commits 0f98a60 and 9c1bc7f; 41f3dd9 (May 11 2026) changed the initial snapshot timeout from 3 min to 1 min but is not the root regression. The underlying issue — that Ptp4lConf: #profile: only appears in logs on the 2nd+ apply — has existed as a latent flake since GetProfileLogID was introduced. Unknown PR for the original introduction; the relevant release branch is release-4.21 in github.com/openshift/ptp-operator.

• Is it a flake? Yes — the test passes when something triggers a second profile application between cluster setup and the ClockSync test window (e.g., operator config reconciliation, hardware config event, daemon restart). In this run, ~2 hours of stability after setup meant no re-apply occurred.

• Suggested Fix: In GetProfileLogID, instead of relying on the Ptp4lConf: log (which requires a second apply), read the ptp4l config file directly from the pod filesystem (/var/run/ptp4l.0.config)


TL;DR: 13 of 15 failures are a single test flake — a log-rotation race that voids GetProfileLogID; 2 are a WPC T-GM holdover hardware failure.



Root Cause Groups:


• 13/15 failures — GetProfileLogID log-rotation timeout (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc): BasicClockSyncCheck → GetClockIDForeign → GetProfileLogID (ptphelper.go:69) opens a Follow: true log stream and searches for (?m).?Ptp4lConf: #profile: (.|\n)?message_tag \[.*\]. That regex only matches a line emitted once by printNodeProfile at daemon startup. Cluster setup finished at ~02:06; ClockSync tests ran at ~04:00–06:00 (~2–4 h later). By then CRI-O log rotation had cycled the startup entry out of the K8s-served log buffer. The snapshot read yields nothing (~26 s); the follow-stream times out after 180 s — producing the observed ~206–218 s failure duration across every suite. The "Can provide a profile with higher priority" variant adds ~60–90 s of profile-apply wait before hitting the same timeout (yielding ~287–298 s).

• 2/15 failures — WPC T-GM DPLL holdover not sustained (tgm): After GNSS disconnect, ts2phc either never emits the "holdover" log token (test 1 — 3+ min of retries, class stays at 6) or emits class-7 followed 7 ms later by class-248 (test 2 — DPLL flips through holdover and drops to FREERUN before the test can assert it). Root is in the WPC DPLL firmware or the ts2phc_parser.go:162-163 holdover-detection logic, not in the test itself.


Cross-Suite Patterns:


SuiteFailuresRoot Cause
bc3Log rotation (GetProfileLogID)
dualfollower3Log rotation (GetProfileLogID)
dualnicbc3Log rotation (GetProfileLogID)
dualnicbcha2Log rotation (GetProfileLogID) — same 206–218 s signature
oc2Log rotation (GetProfileLogID) — same 206–218 s signature
tgm2WPC T-GM holdover hardware/firmware failure

All five non-tgm suites share an identical root cause and near-identical failure durations. The dualnicbcha and oc per-suite analyses characterize the symptom as "LOCKED state timeout," but the timing signature (206–218 s, 287–298 s) and the GetProfileLogID call stack are identical to bc/dualfollower/dualnicbc. tgm is the only suite with a distinct, hardware-level root cause.



Actionable Recommendations:


1. Fix GetProfileLogID to not depend on rotated startup logs. Instead of parsing the one-shot printNodeProfile startup line, query the current PTP configuration state directly — either from a /metrics endpoint, the PtpConfig CR status, or by triggering a daemon profile-reload (e.g., a no-op annotation update) immediately before the test assertion window. This single fix eliminates 13/15 failures.

2. Investigate the WPC DPLL holdover firmware behavior on cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com. Capture ts2phc raw log output during GNSS disconnect to determine whether the DPLL hardware never enters holdover or enters and exits it within milliseconds. If the latter, check whether the DPLL holdover duration register is being set correctly from ts2phc.holdover config and whether a firmware update is available for the WPC card.

3. Add a canary assertion for daemon log reachability before ClockSync tests. A short pre-check that confirms GetPodLogsRegex can read at least one log line from the daemon container (not the specific startup pattern) would convert a silent 206 s timeout into a fast, labeled skip/infra-failure, making future regressions easier to triage.

Overall Severity: MEDIUM — the dominant failure mode is a pre-existing, deterministic time-dependent flake (not a code regression); the tgm failures indicate a real hardware/firmware problem on one lab node but affect only 2 tests.

TL;DR: 13 of 15 failures are a single test flake — a log-rotation race that voids GetProfileLogID; 2 are a WPC T-GM holdover hardware failure.



Root Cause Groups:


• 13/15 failures — GetProfileLogID log-rotation timeout (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc): BasicClockSyncCheck → GetClockIDForeign → GetProfileLogID (ptphelper.go:69) opens a Follow: true log stream and searches for (?m).?Ptp4lConf: #profile: (.|\n)?message_tag \[.*\]. That regex only matches a line emitted once by printNodeProfile at daemon startup. Cluster setup finished at ~02:06; ClockSync tests ran at ~04:00–06:00 (~2–4 h later). By then CRI-O log rotation had cycled the startup entry out of the K8s-served log buffer. The snapshot read yields nothing (~26 s); the follow-stream times out after 180 s — producing the observed ~206–218 s failure duration across every suite. The "Can provide a profile with higher priority" variant adds ~60–90 s of profile-apply wait before hitting the same timeout (yielding ~287–298 s).

• 2/15 failures — WPC T-GM DPLL holdover not sustained (tgm): After GNSS disconnect, ts2phc either never emits the "holdover" log token (test 1 — 3+ min of retries, class stays at 6) or emits class-7 followed 7 ms later by class-248 (test 2 — DPLL flips through holdover and drops to FREERUN before the test can assert it). TL;DR: WPC T-GM node cnfdf32 DPLL never entered HOLDOVER (clock class 7) after GNSS coldboot.


Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: DPLL fails to reach/maintain clock class 7 (HOLDOVER) after GNSS loss (affects Tests: both)
• Evidence:

```

Test 1 — DPLL stuck at FREERUN for full 200s after GNSS disabled:

Matched line: [ptp4l 248] → GNSS disabled → Clock class not yet 7, retrying... (×32+)

→ GNSS enabled → [FAILED] Timed out waiting for clock class 7 (ptp.go:3802, 3m20s elapsed)


Test 2 — class 7 transient, immediately overtaken by 248:

PtpClockClassChange Event recieved map[metric:6], map[metric:7], map[metric:248]

GnssStateChange Event recieved map[metric:0 notification:FAILURE-NOFIX]

→ STEP: Verifying ClockClass value to 7 → [FAILED] expected a metric [7.000000] but got map[metric:248] (ptp.go:3898)

```

• Root Cause: After GNSS signal loss on node cnfdf32.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com, the WPC hardware DPLL transitions directly from LOCKED to FREERUN (class 248) without sustaining HOLDOVER (class 7). In pkg/event/event.go, clock class 7 requires dpllState == PTP_HOLDOVER; since the DPLL reports FREERUN immediately, that path is never taken. In test 2, HOLDOVER was briefly entered (class 7 visible in the event stream) but exhausted faster than the metric-polling step could verify it — confirming the DPLL holdover window on this hardware is abnormally short.
• Breaking PR/Commit: Unknown — the upstream sync PR #613 (0459bc0, CNF-24996/OCPBUGS-90708, merged 2026-06-23) was an upstream sync to the main branch and does not directly affect the release-4.22 branch under test; no code regression identified.
• Is it a flake? Yes — test 2 shows holdover does occur but transiently; this is a hardware-timing sensitivity, consistent with intermittent failures when DPLL holdover duration is at the margins.
• Suggested Fix: Investigate DPLL holdover configuration on cnfdf32 (check LocalHoldoverTimeout configured for the WPC hardware); if hardware is degraded or misconfigured for holdover, reprovisioning or reconfiguring the node should resolve it. Retry the job to confirm transience.
• Affected tests:
• [It] [tgm-serial] PTP e2e tests WPC GM GNSS signal loss tests Testing WPC T-GM holdover through connection loss [Serial]
• [It] [tgm-serial] PTP e2e tests WPC GM Events verification (V2) Testing T-GM Events on GNSS reboot and recovery [Serial]


Relation Between Groups: Single group — both failures share the same root cause: DPLL on cnfdf32 not sustaining HOLDOVER state long enough after GNSS loss. Test 1 never sees class 7 at all; test 2 sees it transiently. Both are direct manifestations of the same abnormally short holdover window on this hardware.


Per-Version Notes: OCP 4.22 (nightly-2026-06-23-164229) — both failures in the [tgm-serial] suite only; all other suites (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc) show 0 failures and passed cleanly.


Affected Images: image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/openshift-ptp/ptp-operator:4.22, image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/openshift-ptp/linuxptp-daemon:4.22, image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/openshift-ptp/cloud-event-proxy:4.22

Root Cause Groups:


• ~33/38 failures — GM in FREERUN (ts2phc FREERUN while DPLL LOCKED), cascading to all BC/slave sync tests (tgm: 11, dualfollower: 4, dualnicbc + dualnicbcha: ~18 implied)

With cnfdf32's ts2phc stuck in FREERUN, clock class never reaches 6, ptp4l never propagates a valid grandmaster signal downstream, and every test in every suite that waits for slave LOCKED state (ptp4l, phc2sys, cloud-event-proxy metrics) times out. The ens2f0np0 interface on cnfdf31 emitting no openshift_ptp_clock_state metric at all is a downstream symptom of the same GM-side failure.


• 1/38 failures — T-BC topology solver finds no valid hardware solution (all suite, SynchronizedBeforeSuite)

PR #205 (84723c8) merged a new deterministic six-constraint T-BC solver to main. The rdu2.redhat.com CI lab does not expose a matching WPC NIC topology (receiver + 2 same-NIC transmitters + local WPC GM). Solver retries 3× and always returns empty, aborting the entire TBC parallel suite before any test runs.


• ~4/38 failures — Possible secondary: ptp4l PMC protocol regression (bad command: GET / bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET seen in dualnicbc/dualnicbcha logs)

May overlap with the GM-FREERUN group if the release-5.0 image has a ptp4l build regression affecting PMC command parsing, but insufficient evidence to split further without dualnicbc/dualnicbcha suite analyses.



Cross-Suite Patterns:


Root Causedualfolloweralltgmdualnicbcdualnicbcha
GM FREERUN / no LOCKED✓ (4)—✓ (11)✓ (~implied)✓ (~implied)
T-BC solver / no hardware—✓ (1)———
PMC bad commandpartial——✓✓

The GM FREERUN pattern is cross-suite and accounts for the overwhelming majority of failures. The T-BC solver failure is entirely suite-specific (all/TBC parallel) and is a code regression, not an infra issue.



Actionable Recommendations:


1. Investigate cnfdf32 ts2phc immediately (highest leverage — fixes ~33 failures). Check whether the release-5.0 linuxptp-daemon image has a regression in ts2phc startup, holdover recovery, or GNSS lock acquisition. Specifically: compare ts2phc behavior between the last passing nightly and this run; check if the ts2phc termination tests earlier in the serial run leave ts2phc in an unrecoverable state (consider adding a ts2phc process health check/reset in AfterEach).

2. Gate the TBC parallel suite behind a hardware capability check (fixes 1 SynchronizedBeforeSuite abort + unblocks the suite). Add an env-var guard (e.g., ENABLE_TBC_TESTS) or a pre-suite hardware probe before enabling PR #205's T-BC code path in nightly CI. Alternatively, provision T-BC-capable hardware in rdu2.redhat.com and verify the L2 discovery result satisfies all six solver constraints.

3. Audit PMC command handling in the release-5.0 image. The bad command: GET / bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET errors in dualnicbc/dualnicbcha indicate a possible ptp4l build or config regression that could independently block sync negotiation even if ts2phc recovers. Cross-reference with the release-5.0 changelog since the last passing nightly.


Overall Issue Class: test_regression (dominant cause is a release-5.0 image regression in ts2phc state management; secondary is a newly merged test code path incompatible with CI lab hardware)


Overall Severity: CRITICAL — 33+ of 38 failures share a single infra/image root cause; the PTP grandmaster is non-functional, making the entire CI job unreliable as a signal for the release-5.0 branch.




Per-Suite Details



dualfollower



Suite: dualfollower (4 failures)


Suite TL;DR: All 4 dualfollower tests fail because node cnfdf31 (the dual-follower slave) never achieves PTP LOCKED state — both follower interfaces (ens2f0np0, ens2f3np3) fail to lock to the upstream grandmaster within the 600s window.


Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: Dual-follower slave node never reached LOCKED state (affects: all 4 tests — "Slave can sync to master", "Dual follower can sync when one follower port goes down", "Can provide a profile with higher priority", "PTP Slave Clock Sync [parallel]")
• Evidence:

```

no Follower port in expected LOCKED state for ptpconfig test-slave1

(node=cnfdf31.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com, label="ptp/clock-under-test",

slaveIfs=[ens2f3np3 ens2f0np0]). Per-interface results:

ens2f3np3: role mismatch (expected=SLAVE, got=LISTENING)

ens2f0np0: clock state metric error: metric: openshift_ptp_clock_state,

nodeName: cnfdf31.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com, aIf: ens2f0np0 not found,

available openshift_ptp_clock_state metri[cs...]

```

```

[dualfollower-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync:

OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out

```

From ptp4l_parser.go:300-305, the LISTENING role with ClockStateFreeRun means ptp4l is running but has not received valid ANNOUNCE messages from any master — the node is waiting for a grandmaster it cannot see. The ens2f0np0 not found in openshift_ptp_clock_state metrics means the daemon published zero clock-state metrics for that interface; ptp4l either never emitted state-change log lines for it, or the metric was never initialised (daemon-side, in log_parsing.go / metrics.go in linuxptp-daemon).


Both symptoms are consistent with the same underlying failure: cnfdf31's dual-follower ptp4l instance never received a PTP ANNOUNCE from the grandmaster on either upstream port, causing it to remain in LISTENING/FREERUN throughout the entire 600s timeout window.


• Root Cause: The dual-follower slave node cnfdf31 could not lock to the PTP grandmaster. ens2f3np3 sat in LISTENING state (ptp4l running, no master discovered), and ens2f0np0 produced no openshift_ptp_clock_state metric at all — indicating the daemon never processed any state-change event for that interface. This is consistent with a network path or grandmaster availability problem at test start, or with a ptp4l-level regression preventing slave negotiation. Notably, other suites in the same CI run show a separate but related symptom: bad command: GET / bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET from PMC across dualnicbc/dualnicbcha, suggesting possible ptp4l protocol-level issues in the release-5.0 image under test.

• Breaking PR/Commit: Unknown. The backport-check script (scripts/check_backport.py) was not present in the workspace. The release-5.0 linuxptp-daemon image is built from the openshift/ptp-operator release-5.0 branch (confirmed: PTP_UNDER_TEST_BRANCH=release-5.0, USE_UPSTREAM=false → build exits before building upstream daemon). Recent commits to release-5.0 of openshift/ptp-operator or its vendored linuxptp binary should be investigated.

• Is it a flake? Possibly — the clean LISTENING state (not a crash, just no master seen) is consistent with a transient network/grandmaster availability issue. However, the suite-wide failure pattern across dualnicbc/dualnicbcha (PMC bad command errors) and tgm (clock class never reaches 6) in the same job run suggests a systemic problem in the release-5.0 production image rather than a one-node flake.

• Suggested Fix: First retry the job to distinguish infrastructure flake from code regression. If the PMC bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET errors in other suites reproduce, audit recent commits to the release-5.0 branch of openshift/ptp-operator and its vendored ptp4l/pmc binary for protocol-compatibility changes; in particular, verify that pmc GET PARENT_DATA_SET still works correctly against the ptp4l version in the built image.

Suite Issue Class: test_failure (slave node



TL;DR: Five deterministic TBC regressions from PR #205 dominate; remaining 4 failures split across DPLL hardware and infra flakes.



Root Cause Groups:


• 5/9 failures — TBC test-code regression (PR #205, aede1e9, Jun 23 2026) — [tbc-serial] suite only. Two sub-causes, both introduced in the same commit:
• Profile discovery nil / log-stream timeout (2 failures): testconfig returns nil for release-4.22's naming convention → ptpConfig is nil panic and regex never matches daemon logs → context deadline exceeded.
• pmc exec split-argument bug (1+ failures): getClockIDViaPMC passes "GET" and "PARENT_DATA_SET" as two separate exec-slice elements; pmc rejects each as bad command, so getClockIDViaPMC times out after 203 s and the priority-profile test never gets a foreign clock ID.
• (The TBC suite TL;DR also attributes failures to PR #618 phc2sys delayed-startup backport interacting with these test bugs, potentially accounting for remaining tbc failures.)

• 2/9 failures — T-GM DPLL skips HOLDOVER, stays at clock class 248 — [tgm-serial] suite only. After GNSS disruption the WPC T-GM DPLL transitions directly to FREERUN/INVALID instead of HOLDOVER, so updateGMState() never sets clockClass = 7. Could be a release-4.22 DPLL driver regression (candidate: PR #617 / fd6ff1e upstream-sync-2026-06-30) or a lab hardware/firmware issue on the T-GM node.

• 2/9 failures — Transient infra flakes — one per suite (bc, dualnicbcha):
• bc: Prometheus cadvisor query returns no valid data after 3 retries for master3.
• dualnicbcha: Kubernetes log-stream returns context deadline exceeded before phc2sys HA failover regex is matched. (Same error signature also appears in tbc, reinforcing the infra-blip explanation for those log-stream timeouts.)


Cross-Suite Patterns:


PatternSuites
context deadline exceeded log-stream timeoutdualnicbcha, tbc (and possibly bc indirectly)
TBC test-code bugs (PR #205)tbc only — suite-specific regression
DPLL FREERUN instead of HOLDOVERtgm only — suite-specific
Prometheus unavailabilitybc only — suite-specific flake

The context deadline exceeded pattern crosses dualnicbcha and tbc, but in tbc it is at least partially caused by PR #205's broken regex derivation (no match → timeout), while in dualnicbcha it appears to be a pure timing/infra blip.



Actionable Recommendations:


1. Fix PR #205 TBC test bugs (highest ROI — unblocks 5/9 failures):
• In test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go getClockIDViaPMC, join "GET" and "PARENT_DATA_SET" into a single string argument: []string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"} (or the correct single-token form that pmc accepts).
• In test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go, add a nil-guard that skips TBC tests when no matching ptpConfig is discovered under release-4.22's naming convention, rather than proceeding to a failing Expect.

2. Investigate the T-GM DPLL HOLDOVER regression (unblocks 2/9 failures):
• Compare release-4.22 linuxptp-daemon DPLL driver commits since the last passing run (focus on dpll.go state-machine transitions around DPLL_FREERUN / DPLL_HOLDOVER).
• If no code change is found, re-run the job on the same T-GM lab node to determine whether this is a persistent hardware/firmware issue.

3. Harden retry logic for transient flakes (prevents future bc/dualnicbcha noise):
• Increase prometheusQueryRetries from 3 → 10 and the retry interval from 10 s → 30 s in testPtpCpuUtilization.
• Wrap the log-stream read in the phc2sys HA failover test with a retry loop (or increase its context timeout) to tolerate brief API-server connection blips.


Overall Issue Class: test_regression


Overall Severity: HIGH — 5 of 9 failures are deterministic regressions blocking the entire TBC serial suite on every run; 2 more are potentially a software regression in the DPLL driver affecting T-GM holdover validation.




Per-Suite Details



bc



Suite: bc (1 failures)


Suite TL;DR: The single bc-parallel failure is a transient Prometheus query timeout — the CPU utilization soak test exhausted all 3 retries trying to fetch cadvisor metrics for master3 from the in-cluster Prometheus pod, which returned no valid data.


Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: Prometheus query returned no valid response after all retries (affects: [It] [bc-parallel] Soak testing PTP CPU Utilization)
• Evidence:

```

CPU usage query failed after 3 attempts: failed to get total cpu usage for ptp pods on node

master3.ptpcimno.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com: prometheus query failure: failed to get a

(valid) response from prometheus

```

(junit-failures.txt, lines 1–7)

• Root Cause: testPtpCpuUtilization (test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go) calls RetryCpuUsageCheck with prometheusQueryRetries=3 and a pkg.Timeout10Seconds retry interval. Each attempt calls isCpuUsageThresholdReachedInPtpPods → GetPodTotalCpuUsage → RunPrometheusQueryWithRetries (test/pkg/metrics/prometheus.go), which runs curl -s http://localhost:9090/api/v1/query inside the Prometheus pod via exec. All three outer retries failed for master3, ultimately returning fmt.Errorf("CPU usage query failed after %d attempts: %w", retries, queryErr). The most common causes are: Prometheus not yet having cadvisor scrape data for that node's new pods, a brief Prometheus pod restart, or an exec timeout. The node itself was Ready throughout the run (confirmed in build log: [INFO] All 6 nodes are Ready).
• Breaking PR/Commit: Unknown — no code change in main or release-4.22 is implicated; the failure is infrastructure-transient.
• Is it a flake? Yes — transient Prometheus unavailability / missing cadvisor samples is a well-known intermittent condition in this suite.
• Suggested Fix: Increase prometheusQueryRetries in testPtpCpuUtilization from 3 to at least 5–10, and/or lengthen the retryInterval from pkg.Timeout10Seconds to 30 s so the cadvisor scrape has time to populate between attempts (test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go).

Suite Issue Class: test_flake

Suite Severity: LOW

Version: 5.0 | Total failures: 32 | Suites: dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tgm



TL;DR: All 32 failures trace to a single unlocked T-GM (ts2phc FREERUN) and a broken pmc command interface cascading across every suite.



Root Cause Groups:


• ~19/32 failures — T-GM ts2phc stuck in FREERUN (clockClass 248) while dpll=LOCKED (tgm: 10, dualnicbc: ~5, dualnicbcha: ~4): The GM node cnfdf32 never emits clockClass 6 because ts2phc_parser.go accumulates "source ts not valid" hits and forces ts2phcState = PTP_FREERUN, overriding a confirmed dpll LOCK. This starves every downstream suite — BC slave ports on the dualnic nodes have no locked upstream grandmaster to sync to, so they remain MASTER/FREERUN themselves, cascading into all WPC GM state, holdover, recovery, and event-timeout failures across all three suites.

• ~13/32 failures — pmc rejects GET PARENT_DATA_SET as two "bad command" tokens (dualnicbc: 5, dualnicbcha: 4, cross-suite overlap ~4): Tests calling ptptesthelper.go:106 via pmc interactive mode receive bad command: GET / bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET for every query, blocking all clock-identity discovery. The two-token error pattern is diagnostic of either (a) the unpinned linuxptp RPM in Dockerfile.ocp updating to ≥4.2 where management_enabled=0 is the new default, or (b) a code path in pmc.go passing "GET PARENT_DATA_SET" as a single unsplit argument to exec.Command. This blocks "Slave can sync to master", "Downstream slave can sync to BC master", and "higher priority" tests in both dualnic suites.

• Suite-specific: No failures appear to be genuinely isolated to a single suite; all are manifestations of the two root causes above.


Actionable Recommendations:


1. Fix the T-GM ts2phc FREERUN (highest leverage — unblocks ~19 failures across all suites): On node cnfdf32, determine whether a recent linuxptp update changed the ts2phc log format so that regularTS2PhcRegex in ts2phc_parser.go:14–23 no longer matches, causing silent NoSourceTSCount accumulation. If the regex is the cause, update it to match the new format. Also verify whether commit fd6ff1e (upstream-sync, merged 2026-06-30 on main) was cherry-picked to release-5.0 and introduced a regression in the ts2phc state machine.

2. Fix the pmc GET PARENT_DATA_SET command breakage (unblocks ~13 failures in dualnic suites): Pin the linuxptp RPM to a known-working version in linuxptp-daemon/addons/redhat/Dockerfile.ocp (currently yum install linuxptp with no version). As a parallel fix, verify that pmc.go and ptptesthelper.go:106 pass GET and PARENT_DATA_SET as separate arguments to exec.Command rather than as a single space-delimited string. Additionally, explicitly set management_enabled 1 in the ptp4l config template in pkg/daemon/config.go to prevent linuxptp ≥4.2 from silently disabling management queries.

3. Investigate whether fd6ff1e needs a backport or revert on release-5.0: Run python scripts/check_backport.py /tmp/ci-investigate fd6ff1e release-5.0 (once available) to confirm whether the 2026-06-30 upstream-sync commit is present in the 5.0 image. If it introduced the ts2phc parser regression or the pmc argument bug, revert or cherry-pick the targeted fix to release-5.0 rather than carrying the full sync.

TL;DR: Cluster log-stream collapse + API auth expiry wiped 22 of 24 tests; a linuxptp-daemon state-machine regression caused the remaining 2 TGM holdover failures.



Root Cause Groups:


• 12/24 failures — linuxptp-daemon log stream unreachable (ClockSync GetProfileLogID/GetClockIDForeign timeout): All ClockSync tests in bc (3), dualfollower (3), dualnicbc (3), dualnicbcha (2), and oc-serial test 1 (1) hit could not find regex in log stream … error reading from stream: context deadline exceeded or timedout waiting for matches. The test helper opens a live kubectl logs --follow stream and waits for a ptp4l profile or sync line that never arrives within 3–10 minutes. Two compounding factors: (a) ptp4l may not be reaching SLAVE state cluster-wide (no grandmaster reachable or log format changed by PR #613), and (b) when the API server began degrading, streaming connections were silently severed rather than cleanly refused.

• 10/24 failures — Kubernetes API server Unauthorized mid-run (oc-serial tests 2–11): After the first oc-serial test completed at ~07:29 UTC, the kubeconfig credentials expired or the API server rejected them (Unauthorized / couldn't get current server API group list: the server has asked for the client to provide credentials). Every subsequent test aborted immediately at the DaemonSet readiness check (linuxptp-daemon DaemonSet must exist before readiness wait → Unauthorized). One variant also showed dial tcp 10.8.34.117:6443: connection refused, indicating the API server briefly went fully unreachable.

• 2/24 failures — TGM holdover state-machine regression (tgm suite): Both T-GM holdover tests fail deterministically: disabling GNSS causes ts2phcState to be forced to PTP_FREERUN (not PTP_HOLDOVER) when NoSourceTSCount == 2 in linuxptp-daemon/pkg/event/event.go:402–403, making ClockClass 7 unreachable. Test 1 exhausted its 3-minute poll; test 2 observed map[metric:248] (freerun) throughout the 10-second sampling window. This is a deterministic regression, not a flake.
